KEY FEATURES

A record of the environment.
Ready for a closer look.

Record temperature and relative humidity locally, then retrieve the data with PC software when your recording period is complete.

80,000-reading memory

Onboard storage keeps readings with the logger throughout the recording task.

Customizable recording interval

Set the data collection interval to suit your storage, transport or observation task. Readings are stored with timestamps.

Temperature + humidity

Published typical accuracy: ±0.2°C for temperature and ±2% RH for relative humidity.

Free PC software

Retrieve data via USB, inspect the curves and export PDF/CSV files locally.

IP55 enclosure

A protected housing for storage and transport recording applications.

Battery-powered recording

A non-replaceable battery supports standalone operation. Match the recording plan to confirmed runtime.

POSITION & RECORDING PLAN

Record the right place.
Keep the context with the data.

Keep the sensing openings exposed to the air you want to record. Secure the logger at an approved location, clear of the object itself, direct sunlight and unintended heat sources. For packed goods, record the air within the selected packaging space and keep a separate note of the crate or shipment identity.

SET UP · RECORD · READ OUT

Let the logger record.
Return to the data.

Set the data collection interval to match the changes you want to observe, then plan the recording period and retrieval date. H100 stores a local history that you can compare with handling, room-operation and shipment notes after downloading.

01

Configure the logger

Set your preferred data collection interval through the supported NFC configuration app. Verify the clock and recording settings before placing H100.

02

Place it and record

Secure the logger at the location you need to assess. It stores temperature and humidity readings with timestamps.

03

Retrieve on your PC

Connect via USB, read the records in free PC software, review the curves and save PDF/CSV exports.

RECORDING INTERVAL & BATTERYSet the interval for your recording task.

Non-replaceable battery. Match the selected recording profile and expected operating conditions to the planned task duration.

01Museums & Collections6 recording tasks +

Build a history of the air surrounding collections, from public galleries to enclosed cases. Review downloaded records against the conservator’s material-specific objectives and exhibition schedule.

Loan Exhibition Galleries

Record air temperature and relative humidity over the exhibition period. Evaluate the timing, duration and frequency of departures from the conditions agreed for the specific loan.+

A loan exhibition needs a record of the environment experienced during installation, public opening and overnight closure. Place identified loggers beside collection zones to reveal differences that a single wall reading can miss. Retrieve the onboard records into local PC software at agreed checkpoints, then compare daily variation with the lender’s conditions and the gallery’s operating notes before planning adjustments for the next exhibition.

Conditions to record
Record air temperature and relative humidity over the exhibition period. Evaluate the timing, duration and frequency of departures from the conditions agreed for the specific loan.
Recording point
Choose object-height positions in representative display areas, including interior and perimeter zones. Separate locations affected by entrance activity from the reference area deeper inside the gallery.
Placement & installation
Use a stable freestanding or approved hanging position that leaves the sensing area exposed. Label each logger and photograph its position without touching an exhibited object.
Recording project details
Share the gallery plan, loan dates, agreed environmental criteria and permitted mounting locations. Include logger quantities, recording interval, retrieval checkpoints and the person responsible for local PC review.

Enclosed Display Cases

Measure case air temperature and relative humidity alongside a room reference. Compare variation before and after openings or maintenance, using the case’s own conservation objectives.+

A room can appear stable while the air inside a showcase follows a different pattern. Record the case microclimate and a nearby room reference through openings, lighting schedules and buffer maintenance. After retrieval, the paired time series helps conservators assess how effectively the enclosure moderates room changes and decide when seals or passive humidity buffers deserve inspection. Use the recorded history to plan case maintenance and review the enclosure strategy for future displays.

Conditions to record
Measure case air temperature and relative humidity alongside a room reference. Compare variation before and after openings or maintenance, using the case’s own conservation objectives.
Recording point
Place one logger in the object compartment with clearance from glazing and buffer trays. Position the room reference close to the case, away from direct supply air.
Placement & installation
Arrange installation with the conservator before closing the case. Secure the logger on an inert support, document its location and plan access for scheduled data retrieval.
Recording project details
Provide case dimensions, enclosed materials, opening frequency, lighting hours and any buffer arrangement. Specify access restrictions, target study duration, logger IDs and the local PC download schedule.

Secure to approved fixed supports with safe retrieval access and exposed sensing openings. Map logger ID, aisle, bay and height, then retain positions for repeat campaigns.
Recording project details

ANSWERS FOR YOUR PROJECT

Frequently
asked questions.

Practical answers about local recording, PC retrieval and selecting the right configuration.

Ask about your recording project ↗
What does this data logger record?+

H100 records temperature and relative humidity over time, with a timestamp for each reading. Use it to review conditions during transport or storage of sensitive goods, including food, heritage objects, packaged semiconductors and other temperature- or humidity-sensitive products.

How do I retrieve the data and create a report?+

Connect the logger to your computer via USB and retrieve the records in Hitelecom's free local PC software. The software supports curve analysis and PDF/CSV export, so you can review the history and save files for your own records.

Tell us your PC operating system when enquiring so we can confirm the software version and USB requirements.

How is the logger configured before use?+

Configure H100 using the supported NFC app on a compatible Android or iOS device. The data collection interval is customizable, so set it for your application and verify the clock and recording settings before deployment.

NFC is used for configuration in this workflow. Recorded data is retrieved through USB in local PC software.

Does the logger need a gateway or an internet connection?+

It records temperature and humidity locally in its onboard memory. Data retrieval uses a USB connection and local PC software, so the recording workflow operates independently of a network connection.

Choose this workflow for a history that your team collects on site or after a journey. The product has no wireless data upload or remote alert service.

Can I set the collection interval, and how long can H100 record?+

Yes. The H100 data collection interval is customizable. Choose an interval that captures the changes relevant to your storage, transport or observation task. The onboard capacity is 80,000 readings; total recording duration depends on the interval and how the supplied configuration counts stored readings.

Share your preferred interval and required recording period with Hitelecom. We can confirm the available settings and help plan USB retrieval for your project.

Where should I place the logger for useful records?+

Place it where the conditions you want to assess occur, and secure it so it stays in that position. For general ambient records, avoid unintended influence from heat sources, direct sunlight or contact with a very hot or cold surface.

In a large room or uneven load, use several locations or a mapping study to understand differences across the space. Keep a note of each logger's location so the exported history has context.

How should I plan battery life for a recording task?+

The logger has a non-replaceable battery. Confirm expected runtime for your selected configuration and plan recording and retrieval around the intended deployment.

Include the recording interval, operating temperature and task duration in your enquiry. For another deployment, save the existing records and check that the remaining battery life covers the next task.

What accuracy and measurement range should I specify?+

The published typical accuracy is ±0.2°C and ±2% RH. Choose a measurement range that covers the lowest and highest conditions expected during your task, and define the accuracy you need at the relevant operating points.

Send those conditions with your enquiry so Hitelecom can confirm the H100 sensing range and accuracy for your application.

What calibration documents should I request?+

State the temperature and humidity points you need checked, the required certificate or traceability, and your recalibration policy when enquiring. Hitelecom can confirm the available documentation for the selected configuration.

For controlled processes, keep the relevant calibration documents with the logger identity and exported records as part of your own quality procedure.

What should I include when specifying H100 for my project?+

Share the application, expected temperature and humidity conditions, preferred collection interval and required recording period. Include the number of recording points, approved placement, local PC environment and any calibration-document requirements.

For a shipment, add the journey stages and planned USB readout at arrival. For a room or storage study, include a location plan and retrieval schedule. Hitelecom can then confirm the H100 configuration and prepare a quotation.
